messages.subject: Re: batch effect MSstats handled ?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ju,

One additional note to point out - your normalization strategy depends on your assumptions.  For example, median normalization assumes most of the proteins in the experiment are the same and have the same concentration for all of the runs.  So if you're performing a more targeted experiment (e.g. a targeted SRM experiment) where you expect a majority of the proteins to change in concentration across conditions, median normalization is not ideal because it may remove the biological effects that you intended to study.

I would take a look at the table in step 20 of section "Procedure 1: MSstatsShiny analysis pipeline" in this paper <https://www.nature.com/articles/s41596-024-01000-3#Sec20>.  For each normalization method within MSstats, it documents the experiment assumptions to consider before employing the method.

Tony

Non-independence means that they way you sample from a tissue for the first MS run affects the way you sample the tissue for the second MS run, e.g. sampling one area of the tissue for the first MS run, then intentionally picking the other side of the tissue for the second MS run. messages.subject: Re: dataprocess error SWATH data
messages.body_plain:
Hi Tony,
Thanks so much for narrowing the issue down! The workflow for this data was:
Generation of an in silico spectral ion library using DIA-NN
Identification/quant of proteins using the SWATH app in Peakview
Conversion of Peakview output files (ion table and FDR table) to MSstats input file using this package https://github.com/bschulzlab/reformatMS
MSstats = dataProcess, groupComparison
This is the workflow used by the core facility I've been working with, and does not show the issue I reported above (dataprocess runs without error, allowing progression on to group comparison). In the end, I figured out this was most likely due to the msstats version they are using (v2.4), while I'm using v4.14. I needed to rerun the code because in addition to the group comparison, I wanted to:
include proteins found only in one condition
extract quantification values using the msstats quantification() function
I tried running the code on the core computer and from memory this older mststats version would not report proteins only in one condition, and the quantification() function was not supported/available.

My PhD student working on a different project using the same workflow has come up with a workaround, instead using:
 DIA-NN to generate both the in silico ion library and perform the ID and quant
Conversion of DIA-NN output file to MSstats input file using this package https://github.com/MiguelCos/MSstats_labelfree_preprocessing
MSstats = dataProcess, groupComparison, quantification
If you think the issue I encountered with the original workflow is in the conversion step, can you let me know of any other options for converting Peakview output > MSstats input? If there are no good options, I'll also reprocess this data through DIA-NN.

Thanks again for your input, it's so helpful!

Cheers,
Taylor

messages.subject: Re: batch effect MSstats handled ?
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I would advise against applying normalization separately.  If you normalize data separately for each group, you eliminate both technical and biological differences within those groups. However, this leaves the differences between groups intact. This imbalance can make it look like the groups are more different than they actually are, artificially lowering your p-values and leading to an increased number of false positives in your results.

For cases where you expect protein abundance to change for a majority of proteins across conditions, we recommend applying reference-based normalization, i.e. for each run, add a known amount of spike-in reference peptide and normalize with respect to the spike-in reference peptide intensity value.  Of course, this would require you to design your experiment ahead of time to use a spike-in reference peptide.

Tony

Hello Tony (and everyone). It's been some time, but I finally got to implement the suggestions that were given to us in our previous meeting. The most important one was to run our phospho enriched data and our global proteome data SEPARATELY in MaxQuant. From this I was able to get 2 "evidence" files. One from the "enriched/phospho" runs and one from the proteome runs.
Then I created the fasta file using the unique razor leading proteins from the enriched/phospho evidence file:                                                                              unique_protein_ids <- unique(evidence$Leading.razor.protein). I uploaded these proteins to Retrieve/ID mapping | UniProt <https://www.uniprot.org/id-mapping>   and I made sure the "from Database" is UniProtKB AC/ID and the "to Database is UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot". After the mapping was done I downloaded the FASTA file (and it was smaller than last time, but it makes sense since we made it from a smaller evidence file).
I also made two different annotation files, one using the evidence from the enriched/phospho runs and a second one using the evidence from the proteome run. I made sure I removed duplicate rows from both of them.
I believed I was ready to run the suggested code:

 msstats_format_lf_full = MaxQtoMSstatsPTMFormat(

     evidence = evidence, # enriched runs

     annotation = annotationclean, # enriched runs annotation

     fasta = "E:/phospho_all_Zahraas and mine/day2_TMT_PTM_my attempt_Asus_office/Code/idmapping_2024_09_17.fasta",

    fasta_protein_name = "uniprot_ac",

     mod_id = "\\(Phospho \\(STY\\)\\)",

     use_unmod_peptides = FALSE,  # This needs to be changed to FALSE when you have two reports, one for proteome and one for enriched runs

    labeling_type = "LF",

     which_proteinid_ptm = "Proteins",

    evidence_prot = evidence_proteome, # proteome runs

annotation_protein = annotation_proteome # proteome runs

Unfortunately I am getting 2 different concerning messages.
A) This one resembles what I was getting before:
[1] "FASTA file missing 1577 Proteins. These will be removed. This may be due to non-unique identifications."
I am planning to investigate which are these proteins that are missing.

[2] getting this error too (I don't understand at all, did not have this previously and I checked every single file I am using):
Error in data.table::fread(input, showProgress = FALSE, ...) :
  input= must be a single character string containing a file name, a system command containing at least one space, a URL starting 'http[s]://', 'ftp[s]://' or 'file://', or, the input data itself containing at least one \n or \r

The evidence files are too big to upload here but I can upload smaller versions, I guess. Any extra advice will be appreciated. Also, I know I am hoping for too much but if there is any possibility we could meet again it would be great and it would depend on your schedule.

Best,
S

I really value your advice. The experiment I have to analyse have been designed without me so they didn't have added spike-ins at the time. I totally agree with you, in case we cannot make Assumption that : 'Most of the proteins in the experiment are the same'
it is a good way to design a comparison experiment between some background against some treated by adding spike-ins.
I think MSstats is perfect tools for our future analysis well designed, I saw in BOX 2 third option for Normalization with spike-ins.

Many thanks for very useful answer!
Best,
Ju

On Tuesday, January 7, 2025 at 11:25:48 AM UTC-5 antho...@gmail.com wrote:
> Hi,
>
> I would advise against applying normalization separately.  If you normalize data separately for each group, you eliminate both technical and biological differences within those groups. However, this leaves the differences between groups intact. This imbalance can make it look like the groups are more different than they actually are, artificially lowering your p-values and leading to an increased number of false positives in your results.
>
> For cases where you expect protein abundance to change for a majority of proteins across conditions, we recommend applying reference-based normalization, i.e. for each run, add a known amount of spike-in reference peptide and normalize with respect to the spike-in reference peptide intensity value.  Of course, this would require you to design your experiment ahead of time to use a spike-in reference peptide.
>
> Tony
>
> On Thursday, January 2, 2025 at 12:49:06 PM UTC-5 jcard...@gmail.com wrote:
> > Tony, thanks for pointing me that, it is helpful.
> > Box2 : 1.Normalization, table to make correct decision about method to use to normalize.
> > Assumption
> >  "Most of the proteins in the experiment are  the same ..."
> > I can clearly identify that it is NOT my case
> > =  they must be normalized separately.
> >
> > If I do this:
> > summarized_processed_data_background <- MSstats::dataProcess(...)
> > summarized_processed_data_treated <- MSstats::dataProcess(...)
> >
> > Each Condition are normalized separately,  but my problems are:
> > 1. to perform  'groupComparison':
> > input need to have all samples within same summarized object.
> > I coded a method to merge them back together it by myself, but I suspect that MSstats being very versatile, there must be a proper way to address such a case?
> >
> > 2. MSstats is handling batch effect:
> > I understand that it would be the case only if  controls and treated are together when 'dataProcess' method  is applied.
> >
> > So my dilemma is that: how to conceal that:
> > dataProcess method must be applied on my data separeted for normalization,
> > but must be achieve all together for removing batch effect?
> >
> > Many thanks!
> >
> >
> >
> >
> >
> > On Thursday, January 2, 2025 at 11:20:46 AM UTC-5 antho...@gmail.com wrote:
> > > Hi Ju,
> > >
> > > One additional note to point out - your normalization strategy depends on your assumptions.  For example, median normalization assumes most of the proteins in the experiment are the same and have the same concentration for all of the runs.  So if you're performing a more targeted experiment (e.g. a targeted SRM experiment) where you expect a majority of the proteins to change in concentration across conditions, median normalization is not ideal because it may remove the biological effects that you intended to study.
> > >
> > > I would take a look at the table in step 20 of section "Procedure 1: MSstatsShiny analysis pipeline" in this paper <https://www.nature.com/articles/s41596-024-01000-3#Sec20>.  For each normalization method within MSstats, it documents the experiment assumptions to consider before employing the method.
> > >
> > > Tony
> > >
> > > On Wednesday, December 18, 2024 at 5:16:09 PM UTC-5 jcard...@gmail.com wrote:
> > > > I am actually using equalizeMedians parameter. Excellent that it handle Batch effect also!
> > > > I just read that:
> > > > Ref: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.biosystems.2022.104661
> > > >
> > > > Assessing normalization methods in mass spectrometry-based proteome profiling of clinical samples:
> > > > median ... normalization methods performed the best ... minimizing the batch effects in the study and increasing the significance of the relevant known associations found between proteins...
> > > >
> > > > That support also your answer!
> > > >
> > > > Thank you so much for MSstats and for this very fast answer!
> > > >
> > > >
> > > > Ju
> > > >
> > > > On Tuesday, December 17, 2024 at 7:18:27 PM UTC-5 devonj...@gmail.com wrote:
> > > > > Hello,
> > > > >
> > > > > Yep normalization will handle catch effects. The default option is to equalize medians across runs.
> > > > >
> > > > > Devon
> > > > >
> > > > > On Tuesday, December 17, 2024 at 3:43:40 PM UTC-5 jcard...@gmail.com wrote:
> > > > > > Hi,
> > > > > >   Trying to figure out if MSstats is handling batch effect?  Not sure. According to doc
> > > > > > https://mirrors.dotsrc.org/bioconductor-releases/3.12/bioc/manuals/MSstats/man/MSstats.pdf
> > > > > >
> > > > > >  p3
> > > > > > dataProcess()  method perform:
> > > > > >  Normalization: to remove systematic bias between MS runs.
> > > > > >
> > > > > > Is that not definition of batch effect? I want to know if I apply dataProcess() Normalization, I actually do batch effect correction ?
> > > > > >
> > > > > > Many thanks!

To clarify, this FASTA file is obtained by querying Uniprot with all of the protein IDs present in your evidence file.  The reason why this FASTA file is important is because MaxQuant's evidence file does not report the specific amino acid that is modified relative to the whole protein sequence (rather, it reports the specific amino acid relative to the reported peptide).  The FASTA file allows MSstatsPTM to determine the absolute location of the modification relative to the whole protein.

messages.subject: May Institute on Computation and Statistics for Mass Spectrometry
messages.subject_clean: May Institute on Computation and Statistics for Mass Spectrometry
messages.body_plain:
The May Institute on Computation and Statistics for Mass Spectrometry and Proteomics, taking place on April 28 – May 11, 2025 on the campus of Northeastern University in Boston MA, is now accepting applications. The application deadline is March 5, 2025.

Instructors are leading experts, who contributed numerous experimental and computational methods and software. The target audiences are both beginners and experienced scientists, with both experimental and computational expertise.
New this year is a "Future developers meeting", a 2-day program that brings together developers (and aspiring developers) of computational and statistical tools for mass spectrometry, proteomics and metabolomics. We invite you to submit an abstract and present your research.

Participants can select a subset of the following programs:
* April 28 - April 30, Quantitative proteomics with Skyline. Lead instructors: Susan Abbatiello, Brendan MacLean and Lindsay Pino
* April 30 – May 2, Beginners R and beginners statistics. Lead instructor: Ryan Benz
* April 30 – May 2, Intermediate R, data visualization and statistics. Lead instructor: Kylie Bemis
* April 30 – May 2, Intermediate Python, data visualization and statistics. Lead instructors: Ben Gyori, Arzu Tuğçe Güler, and Jeremy Muhlich
* May 5 – May 7, Statistics for quantitative mass spectrometry: methods and case studies. Lead instructors: Olga Vitek and Devon Kohler
* May 7 – May 9, Interpretation of proteomic experiments in the context of biomolecular networks with INDRA. Lead instructor: Ben Gyori
* May 9, Analysis of mass spectrometry images with Cardinal. Lead instructor: Kylie Bemis
* May 10 - May 11, Future Developers Meeting

A limited number of registration fee wavers will be available for students and postdocs affiliated with academic or nonprofit institutions in the US.
Please share this widely. More information is at https://computationalproteomics.khoury.northeastern.edu/

> > > > > Regarding Ivan's question, to clarify what MSstats does, MSstats assumes technical replicates are independent observations.  But also, if 3 technical replicates were extracted from the same tissue, that does not necessarily imply non-independence. messages.subject: Re: Annotation Issue
messages.body_plain:
Hey,

My initial guess is that in your annotation file, you need to remove the extra space between "Report Intensity" and the channel number, i.e. "Reporter Intensity  1" (two spaces) is not the same as "Reporter Intensity 1" (1 space).  And ensure the capitalization is aligned, i.e.  "Reporter intensity" is not equal to "Reporter Intensity".

Other than that, without a subset of your evidence file, it's hard for me to diagnose your actual problem. If you still encounter issues, please send a subset of your evidence file with quantification values.

Tony

The reason why this FASTA file is important is because MaxQuant's evidence file does not report the specific amino acid that is modified relative to the whole protein sequence (rather, it reports the specific amino acid relative to the reported peptide). Hi Marek,

It appears from your data that there may be a couple problems.

First, I do not see which column should correspond to the Intensity. We expect there to be a PeakArea column which we use as protein intensity.

Second, you need to include an annotation file along with this file. The annotation file maps the runs to the condition and bioreplicate. As your condition in the data currently says "No Defined", we would not be able to tell what the experimental design is. There are a variety of resources for how to setup the annotation file, but I would still recommend looking at the end-to-end workflow vignette, <https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/MSstats/inst/doc/MSstatsWorkflow.html> which includes an example of what it should look like.

Devon

messages.subject: Re: Annotation Issue
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

By default, the MaxQuant MsstatsPTM converter uses the ReporterIntensityCorrected column for processing intensity values.  I'm not sure what makes ReporterIntensity vs ReporterIntensityCorrected columns different, but if you prefer to use ReporterIntensity, please let me know and I can look to enable the code to use ReporterIntensity.

Regardless, I looked at your data and the intensities for the norm channel in the ReporterIntensityCorrected column are all <= 1 (and all <= 1 in the ReporterIntensity column with the exception of one row), which leads to all of those values being considered as missing values within MSstatsPTM.  As a result, MSstatsPTM cannot normalize w.r.t. to the norm channel since those values are considered missing.

Out of curiosity, is there any reason why the intensity values in your dataset are so low, especially for the norm channel?

Tony

To clarify, this FASTA file is obtained by querying Uniprot with all of the protein IDs present in your evidence file.  The reason why this FASTA file is important is because MaxQuant's evidence file does not report the specific amino acid that is modified relative to the whole protein sequence (rather, it reports the specific amino acid relative to the reported peptide). messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Could you also attach your annotation file?  That'll make it easier to assess the problem.

>From initial glance, there are 2 criteria that need to be met that your matrix may not be satisfying:
Column names of your matrix must be the same as your condition labels.
The matrix should include all condition labels (i.e. if you have 3 conditions, you'll have 3 columns in your contrast matrix).
Thanks,
Tony
